Minimum wages for sectors like fast food, hotels, or construction don't just raise pay. They create legal boundaries to work around—pushing firms to cut hours, raise prices, reduce service quality, and even reorganize tasks and relabel jobs to escape coverage. The narrower the sector-specific minimum wage, the stronger the incentive for firms and workers to avoid being covered, write Cato's @MrRBourne and Nathan Miller.
